content: MutationObserver cost: subtree:true on document.body is catastrophic on complex pages - every insertion/removal anywhere generates a record; a React re-render touching 500 elements = 500 records; callbacks run as microtasks that block rendering before paint (unpacked.danielhowells.com deep dive, StackOverflow 31659567, whatwg/dom #484). Records hold strong refs to nodes (memory spikes). Best practices verified across sources: scope observation narrowly (childList only, subtree false on direct containers), use attributeFilter for attributes, debounce via rAF/setTimeout, scan ONLY inserted subtrees (OxiCloud commit pattern), disconnect once target found, avoid querySelectorAll and forced layout in callbacks, drain records with takeRecords(). Instagram's infinite feed virtualizes DOM constantly - a body-level observer fires on every scroll batch; observe only the feed container/video insertion points.
